sam_cs: Quick help — Fathom onboarding on AWS Fargate seeing ~30s of 429s right after a new task group scales up. They use the JS SDK and an internal auth proxy that mints short-lived tokens per task. Any fast playbook?
irene_eng: Likely a token-minting stampede. Ask for a few request ids and headers; check X-RateLimit-Remaining.
sam_cs: Customer logs (sanitized):
2024-08-24T10:12:01Z id=tx101 POST /v1/embeddings 200
2024-08-24T10:12:02Z id=tx102 POST /v1/embeddings 429 X-RateLimit-Remaining:0
2024-08-24T10:12:02Z id=tx103 POST /v1/embeddings 429 X-RateLimit-Remaining:0

chao_sre: Fast mitigations to suggest: (1) implement a per-task /tmp token cache with atomic write + TTL check so only the first process mints; (2) add a small randomized startup jitter (0-400ms) before initializing the SDK; (3) if they control deployment, stagger task start or use smaller batch rollout. Also confirm SDK version — older JS SDKs didn't respect single-flight.
irene_eng: Example snippet to share: 
const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random()*400);
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, jitter));
const token = readTmpToken() || (await fetchAndStoreToken());
await Redwood.initialize({ token });

sam_cs: Sent to customer; they applied jitter + tmp-cache and reported 90% fewer 429s immediately. They asked if we can relax server-side limits for onboarding ramps.

chao_sre: Ops can do a manual short onboarding quota bump for verified customers (24-48h) — needs CS request. For product changes like automatic grace windows, file an RFC.

infra-bot: Created ticket CS-13579 to add Fargate warmup patterns to onboarding docs and track quota-bump flow.

sam_cs: Closing thread — will reopen if they regress. Thanks everyone :pray:
